title: Cities five degrees hotter
text: On the hottest afternoons of summer, a city can run five degrees warmer than the countryside around it. The {{1}} is built, not meteorological: asphalt and concrete {{2}} the day's heat and release it all night, buildings block the breezes that would carry it away, and waste heat from traffic and air conditioning {{3}} to the total. The consequences are not evenly shared. Tree-lined wealthy districts stay several degrees cooler than dense, unshaded ones, so the people least able to afford air conditioning {{4}} the most. Simple measures {{5}} surprisingly well: painting roofs white, planting street trees, requiring reflective materials and unsealing the ground so water can {{6}} through it. Medellin in Colombia lowered temperatures in some districts by two degrees with a network of green corridors, for a {{7}} of what a metro line costs. As heatwaves lengthen, city governments have begun treating shade as {{8}} infrastructure — as essential as drainage or street lighting. The old image of the city as a machine for living is giving way to something closer to a forest: cooler, damper and more comfortable precisely where people walk.

gaps.explanation: 'the reason is built, not meteorological' — what explains it; region = an area, regime = a government.
'concrete absorbs the day's heat' — takes it in; adorn = decorate, abhor = detest.
'waste heat adds to the total' — increases it; aid = help (needs an object), arc = curve.
'the people least able to afford air conditioning suffer the most' — endure the harm; profit, gain and benefit reverse it.
'simple measures deliver surprisingly well' — produce the goods; linger = stay on, wither = dry up.
'water can seep through it' — pass slowly through small gaps; seethe = boil with anger, sieve = strain.
'for a tenth of what a metro line costs' — one part in ten; tension = strain, tendon = a body cord.
'treating shade as essential infrastructure' — necessary; essence is the noun and essentially the adverb, but the adjective slot is needed.
